title: Survey Reveals Power of Personality in Getting Hired
paragraphs: When you apply for a job, your skills and experience are obviously important. But according to a new survey, your personality may be just as important, or even more so.

The survey was conducted by The Harris Poll for Express Employment Professionals, a large US staffing company. Between May and June, it asked 1,006 American hiring managers and 1,000 workers and job seekers about the role of personality in hiring.

The results showed that 91% of hiring managers believe personality matters as much as skills. Even more surprisingly, 86% said that the right personality can make up for a gap in a candidate's skills.

Many hiring managers also believe they can judge a person very quickly. About 87% said they can tell from the first conversation whether a candidate will be a good fit for their company. According to the survey, hiring managers also look at things like small talk before an interview, the tone of a candidate's emails, and how candidates treat office staff.
Job seekers seem to be aware of this. Around 94% said companies had judged their personality through informal conversations, reference checks or personality tests.

So which personality traits matter most? Both groups ranked reliability first, chosen by 66% of hiring managers and 65% of job seekers. Honesty came second, followed by adaptability, flexibility and self-motivation.
Personality may also affect how quickly people move up in their careers. Almost all hiring managers, 99%, said a positive or friendly personality can help people advance faster.
Bob Funk Jr., the CEO of Express, said every employee affects the workplace in ways that go beyond the duties listed in their job description.
However, some experts point out that the survey only shows what people believe. It does not check whether first impressions actually predict how well people perform at work.
